requirements.description: Database queries use parameterized queries or safe ORM APIs; untrusted input is never concatenated into a query.
OS commands use an argument vector (no shell string interpolation) and inputs are validated/allowlisted.
Server-side requests to user-influenced URLs enforce an allowlist and block internal/metadata addresses and non-http(s) schemes.
Output is contextually encoded/escaped for the sink (HTML, attribute, JS, URL); no raw interpolation into markup.
Serialized objects from untrusted sources are not deserialized with unsafe loaders (pickle/yaml.load/native unserialize).
File paths built from input are canonicalized and confined to an intended base directory.
A new session identifier is issued on authentication; session IDs are unpredictable and invalidated on logout.
JWTs are verified with an allowlisted algorithm and a trusted key; 'none'/algorithm-confusion and unverified decode are rejected.
Every request enforces object- and function-level authorization against the authenticated principal; identifiers from the client are never trusted for ownership.
Authentication verifies credentials server-side against a trusted store and fails closed on any error.
Cryptography uses approved algorithms and modes with authenticated encryption; keys come from a managed source, never hardcoded.
Weak or broken primitives (MD5, SHA-1, DES, ECB, unauthenticated CTR) are not used for security purposes.
